subject.title: fix(cron): preserve rescheduled reminders after gateway restart

question: After reviewing current-head persisted restart evidence, should the cron owner accept the new behavior that an overdue replacement one-shot survives and catches up after the old active run is repaired?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes how existing persisted one-shot state is interpreted during gateway recovery, and the protected label requires explicit human handling rather than automated cleanup.

options.title: Accept after runtime proof
options.body: Require a redacted terminal trace or runtime log showing a rescheduled persisted one-shot surviving restart and executing exactly once, then review the refreshed head.

options.title: Keep prior recovery semantics
options.body: Decline the behavior change if maintainers do not want overdue replacements to enter startup catch-up after restart.

recommendation.title: Accept after runtime proof
recommendation.body: Require a redacted terminal trace or runtime log showing a rescheduled persisted one-shot surviving restart and executing exactly once, then review the refreshed head.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged and current work both center on cron schedule ownership and restart behavior.
